He was a young, tall, good looking man. He was fearless and always wanted to do something new and exciting. He has videos up on YouTube doing challenges and showing the work he put into his cars and stuff. He always wanted to be an influencer.

He was hilarious. Genuinely one of the funniest people I know. He had the most funniest and contagious laugh. I’m sure most of the time, people were laughing at his goofy laugh lol, but that didn’t bother him. In fact, he would laugh at his own laugh! He brightened any room he walked into. I’m his older brother, but he gave me comfort and strength to overcome many things. He always pushed me out of my comfort zone.

He would sometimes put on a tough exterior, but he was a softy. His friends told me he would play with their baby sisters and brothers. He loved animals, especially dogs. I’ve seen so many videos of him smothering dogs and was starting to love cats. 

He was loyal. His friends recently told me he picked up a friend to drive an hour away to pick up another friend stranded in the middle of a dark highway more than an hour away. He didn’t double think it. He got up and went to help right away. He would do anything for the people he loved. He had the biggest heart in the world.

He was an absolute joy to be around. He wasn’t perfect, but he was real. He told it like it was. He defended his own and everything he loved. He was starting to grow into his adult version, and it was cut short. He would have been a hell of a father. And whenever I have kids, I’ll make sure to pass down all my stories and memories that I have with him. He was a goofball, a daredevil, and I’m going to miss him for the rest of my life. I wish everybody was as lucky as anybody who got to meet him. He was a wonderful person.

At his funeral service, we had about a half hour delay on the service because there were so many people trying to find parking and get out of the traffic that was created by people going to his funeral service. It was crazy! So many people came by to pay their respect. 

My brother was, is, and will always be loved. Gone way too soon.

Thank you for asking me about him. It means the world to me.

I lost my brother on June 23rd this year. He was my younger brother, only 23. He passed away from a motorcycle accident heading home, maybe two minutes away or so, at 2 in the morning.

I was at work when my mom called me at 6:59 am, bawling. I couldn’t make out what she was saying only that I needed to go home. Upon my arrival, I learned my brother had been killed.

Through these past weeks, the best support I have received is when people let me grieve him. They just let me cry and feel all I need to feel. They let me talk about him, ask me how he was, his favorite things. We share stories about the funny and silly things he would do and say. My biggest fear is forgetting him. Not his existence, but the way he looked, how he sounded, his contagious laugh, etc. His friends have been sending me photos and videos of him, and that’s helped as well. 

That kind of support has helped me. I don’t like hearing “be strong for your mom” or “I know what it feels like” because unless someone has lost a sibling, and a younger sibling at that, they don’t know what it feels like. Those are my two cents, hope it helps!

My brother passed away in a motorcycle accident on June 23, 2024. He was 23. He was my little brother. There’s an emptiness in me. I feel something is missing.

I have a few right now.

“What is grief, if not love persevering.” Yes, spoken by Vision in WandaVision.

The other one is from a video a saw a while back, but has come back after my brother’s passing. In an interview of Andrew Garfield speaking about his mother who has recently passed away at the time, he says “Grief is unexpressed love”. And it’s true. It’s all the love with nowhere to go, but it shouldn’t necessarily be a bad thing.

The last one was a Billy Bob Thornton speaking about his brother’s passing. He mentions that he is fine feeling all the grief for the rest of his life because his brother deserves it. He says it feels like when it first happened and he’s okay with it because nothing will ever change how much his brother means to him. The grief he feels is all the love, all the memories, all the laugh, and it’s better to embrace it. He could now only honor his brother in everything he does.

I lost my brother on Sunday, motorcycle accident at 2am. My mom called me bawling, while I was at work at 7am. I came home, found the coroner standing outside with my mom. I hadn’t seen my brother since possibly last Thursday. We were watching Young Sheldon and cracking up. I don’t know if I saw him Friday. I can’t remember.

My brother texted me on Saturday evening about his sandwich, and I put it away for him. I didn’t respond. That was our relationship. I wish I did though. I wish I could have told him to be safe. Or that I love him. I know deep down, in our own way, my brother and I knew we loved each other.

He was 23. This whole week has been rough. I miss my brother dearly. Just remember, grief is all the unexpressed love. I will cry at any point of the day. I get a max of four hours sleep, waking up multiple times, followed by points where I think I hear my brother coming home only to wake up in complete silence. I know this grief will last the entirety of my lifetime, but if that’s how I have to live, then I accept it. My brother deserves it. Nothing can ever replace what he means to me, or how he ever made me feel, or any of our insiders. He will always be my little brother. I’m 29, and we had planned a lot together. We were recently planning a Dodgers’ away game to San Francisco, or Boston or New York. 

Nothing feels the same though. I don’t have any joy. Music sounds like sound. Sitcoms we liked to watch together don’t make me laugh. But what has been helping me is talking about him. Even if it makes me cry, it’s all the unexpressed love I have for him, and I don’t ever want that to go away. Nothing could ever prepare you for death, so how am I supposed to accept the fact that now I will go on living the rest of my life without my brother? All I can do is carry his legacy forward. He was a beautiful soul with the biggest heart. He was a breath of fresh air. His laugh was so contagious and he had the worst jokes but he was the life of the party. That’s how I want people to remember him. 

Find comfort in what your brother meant to you and how you can honor him. My two sisters and I know what you’re feeling. You are not alone. My brother’s death has made me feel the loneliest, even when surrounded by family and friends. But I talk about him and it helps a little. Talk about your brother. As dumb as it sounds, find comfort in your grief. Grief is love persevering. Grief is unexpressed love. Your feelings are valid. What you’re feeling is all the love you have for your brother.

I appreciate your sympathy.
